outcomes.text: With guidance, demonstrate how to operate a computing device.
With guidance, use appropriate terminology to locate and identify common computing devices and components in a variety of environments (e.g. turn on, navigate, open/close programs/apps).
With guidance, correctly use software that controls computing devices (e.g. e.g. programs, browsers, websites, and applications).

subtopics.title: With guidance, identify and apply basic input/output skills

outcomes.text: Input (keyboarding, mouse, touchscreen, voice, camera, interactive board)
Output (monitor, screen, printer, audio).
Recognize that computing systems might not work as expected and with guidance can identify simple hardware or software problems (e.g. volume turned down on headphones, monitor turned off).
Recognize that computing devices are connected via wired or wireless networks so that they can communicate with each other.

Know that the computing device can save information as data that can be searched, modified, and saved or deleted (e.g. save photos, files, or videos).
Students understand that data about themselves and the world around them is collected, used, and organized in a meaningful way.

Understand different ways in which types of technologies are used in your daily life.
With guidance understand what would be appropriate while participating in an online environment. (Digital Citizenship - focus on Digital Literacy).
Understand that computing technology has changed and improved the way people live, work, and interact.
With guidance understand responsible digital citizenship (legal and ethical behaviors) in the use of technology systems and software.
Discuss the fact that a wide range of jobs require knowledge or use of computer science.
